question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

I thought of this idea / just when you called / me yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "I thought of this idea just when you called me yesterday" is grammatically complete and correct. Every part follows standard usage.

◦ "I thought of this idea" — correct past tense (think – thought – thought).

◦ "just when you called" — correct use of "when" as a conjunction with the past tense.

◦ "me yesterday" — correct object pronoun "me" + adverb of time "yesterday".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The verb "think of" (to conceive/imagine an idea) is the correct phrasal usage here.

• Both actions ("thought" and "called") happened in the past, and the tenses agree, so there is no error.

NOTE

• In "spot the error" questions, first check subject–verb agreement, tense consistency, prepositions and pronouns. When all four parts are correct, the answer is No error.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Fish live in aquariums and pigs live in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sties.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "sty" (plural "sties") is the pen or enclosure where pigs are kept. So "pigs live in sties". (सूअरबाड़ा)

◦ Correct: Fish live in aquariums and pigs live in sties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "stables" — homes for horses.

• Option 2 "dens" — homes for wild animals like lions/foxes.

• Option 4 "kennels" — shelters for dogs.

NOTE

• Animal dwellings (SSC favourite): horse–stable, dog–kennel, pig–sty, bird–nest/aviary, bee–hive, cow–byre/shed, hen–coop, lion–den, rabbit–burrow, eagle–eyrie.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Mountaineering requires a combination of physical strength, endurance, technical skill and mental fortitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. timidity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fortitude" means courage and mental strength in facing pain, danger or difficulty. Its antonym is "timidity", meaning lack of courage or confidence; fearfulness. (धैर्य/साहस का विलोम — कायरता/भीरुता)

◦ Example: Her fortitude in adversity was admirable, unlike his timidity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "persistence" and Option 3 "enthusiasm" are closer to positive qualities, not opposites of fortitude.

• Option 1 "excitement" is unrelated to courage.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fortitude: courage, grit, resilience, endurance, bravery. Antonyms: timidity, cowardice, weakness, faint-heartedness.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

The man had committed a grave offence so he was granted bail.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. trivial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Grave" (as an adjective) means very serious, severe or important. Its antonym is "trivial", meaning of little importance; minor. (गंभीर का विलोम — तुच्छ/मामूली)

◦ Example: It was a grave mistake, not a trivial one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "serious" and Option 4 "solemn" are synonyms of grave.

• Option 2 "dignified" (having a serious, respectable manner) is unrelated as an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of grave: serious, solemn, critical, severe. Antonyms: trivial, trifling, minor, insignificant.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank to complete the idiom and make the sentence meaningful.

Her company's new product launch was a real ___________________ squib.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. damp.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a damp squib" means something that is much less impressive or exciting than expected; a disappointing failure. (उम्मीद से कमज़ोर/निराशाजनक साबित होना)

◦ Correct: Her company's new product launch was a real damp squib.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• A "squib" is a small firework; if it becomes damp (wet), it fails to explode — hence the imagery of a let-down.

• "dirty squib", "deaf squib" and "dear squib" are not idioms.

NOTE

• Similar idioms for failure/disappointment: "fall flat", "fizzle out", "come to nothing", "an anticlimax".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Radha stepped backward to avoid the incoming traffic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Forward.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Backward" means towards the back / in the direction behind one. Its antonym is "forward", meaning towards the front / ahead. (पीछे की ओर का विलोम — आगे की ओर)

◦ Example: He took a step backward, then moved forward again.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Affront" (an insult) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Beside" (next to) and Option 4 "Behind" (at the back of) are prepositions of place, not the true opposite of "backward" as a direction.

NOTE

• Directional pairs: backward ↔ forward, upward ↔ downward, inward ↔ outward, left ↔ right.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Naviggetion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Naviggetion" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Navigation", meaning the process of accurately ascertaining one's position and planning/following a route (of a ship, aircraft, etc.). (मार्ग-निर्धारण/नौसंचालन)

◦ Spelling key: NA + VI + GA + TION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Strengthen" (to make stronger), "Cleansing" (making clean) and "Comparison" (act of comparing) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Common trap: the sound "-gation" is spelt with a single "g" and "a" — navigation, not "naviggetion". Related: navigate (verb), navigator (noun).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Riside.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Riside" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Reside", meaning to live in a particular place. (निवास करना)

◦ Spelling key: RE + SIDE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Scatter" (to throw about/disperse), "Resort" (to turn to / a holiday place) and "Scarf" (a piece of cloth worn around the neck) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related to reside: resident (noun), residence (place of living), residential (adjective). Note the "e", not "i", in the first syllable.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please pass _________ the salt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs the indirect object of "pass", which must be an object pronoun. "me" is the object form of "I". So "Please pass me the salt". (कर्म कारक — me)

◦ Correct: Please pass me the salt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "my" and Option 2 "mine" are possessives (my salt / it is mine).

• Option 3 "I" is a subject pronoun, not an object.

NOTE

• Pronoun forms: subject (I) – object (me) – possessive adjective (my) – possessive pronoun (mine). After a verb/preposition, use the object form: "pass me", "give her", "tell them".

question:
The given sentence is divided into three segments. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If there is no error, select 'No error' as your answer.

Meenu looks/ much better/ today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Meenu looks much better today" is grammatically correct.

◦ "Meenu looks" — correct subject + linking verb ("looks" agrees with the singular subject).

◦ "much better" — "much" is the correct intensifier before the comparative "better" (we say "much better", not "very better").

◦ "today" — correct adverb of time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Look" here is a linking verb followed by an adjective ("better"), which is standard.

• Comparatives are intensified by "much / far / a lot", never by "very": much better, far worse.

NOTE

• When every segment is correct, the answer is No error. Remember: "much/far + comparative" is correct; "very + comparative" is wrong.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

My cousin thinks that / English is difficult / than other subjects.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. English is difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" later in the sentence signals a comparison, so the adjective must be in the comparative degree — "more difficult", not "difficult". The error lies in the segment "English is difficult".

◦ Correct: My cousin thinks that English is more difficult than other subjects.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "than other subjects" is correct once the comparative is used.

• Long adjectives form the comparative with "more": more difficult, more beautiful, more important.

NOTE

• Whenever "than" appears, check that a comparative ("-er" or "more ...") precedes it. "Difficult than" → "more difficult than".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

It was an insight / and determination of the lady doctor / that people were / able to lead a normal life.
option_2: able to lead a normal life
option_4: and determination of the lady doctor
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. It was an insight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence refers to a specific, particular insight of the lady doctor, so the definite article "the" is required, not the indefinite "an". The error is in "It was an insight" — it should be "It was the insight".

◦ Correct: It was the insight and determination of the lady doctor that people were able to lead a normal life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• A defining relative clause ("that people were able to lead a normal life") points to a specific quality, which calls for "the".

• The other segments are grammatically acceptable.

NOTE

• Use "the" for something specific/already identified; use "a/an" for something general or mentioned for the first time. Here the insight is specified by the following clause, so "the" is correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Pull someone's leg
option_2: To physically pull the legs of a person
option_3: To take a situation seriously or earnestly
option_4: To tease or play a joke on someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To tease or play a joke on someone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "pull someone's leg" means to tease or fool someone in a light-hearted, joking way. (किसी की टाँग खींचना — मज़ाक करना)

◦ Example: Don't take him seriously; he's just pulling your leg.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Idioms are non-literal, so Option 2 (the literal meaning) is a distractor.

• Options 1 and 3 have no connection to the idiom.

NOTE

• Similar "joke/tease" idioms: "have someone on", "wind someone up", "take the mickey". Do not confuse with "pull one's socks up" (to make an effort to improve).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramesh is fond at playing guitar in his free time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "fond" is always followed by the preposition "of". So "fond of playing guitar" is correct, not "fond at". (का शौकीन होना)

◦ Correct: Ramesh is fond of playing guitar in his free time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "fond of" is a fixed prepositional collocation — it takes a noun or a gerund (fond of music / fond of playing).

• "fond at / for / on / in" are all incorrect.

NOTE

• Adjective + preposition collocations (SSC favourite): fond of, afraid of, good at, interested in, proud of, keen on, tired of.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

I did not _______ that he would ______ the offer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. expect; accept.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs "expect" (to anticipate/think likely) in the first blank and "accept" (to agree to receive/take) in the second. (उम्मीद करना; स्वीकार करना)

◦ Correct: I did not expect that he would accept the offer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "except" (a preposition meaning "apart from") is a homophone confused with "accept" (to receive) — Option 1 wrongly uses "except".

• "bate" (to lessen/hold back, as in "with bated breath") and "bait" (to lure/a lure) do not fit the meaning of the sentence.

NOTE

• Confusable pairs (SSC): accept (to take) vs except (apart from); expect (to anticipate) vs suspect; bate vs bait.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

Thank you for this jar of asorted cookies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. assorted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "asorted" should be "assorted", meaning of various sorts/kinds mixed together. (विविध प्रकार के / मिले-जुले)

◦ Correct: Thank you for this jar of assorted cookies.

◦ Spelling key: AS + SORT + ED (double "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "esorted", 2 "essorted" and 3 "asoted" are all wrong spellings.

NOTE

• Related words: assortment (noun — a mixed collection), sort (to arrange). Remember the double "s": as-sorted.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form.

I shall come again in the afternoon for lunch.
option_1: I will be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.
option_2: I shall have come again in the afternoon for lunch
option_3: I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.
option_4: I will come again in the afternoon for lunch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The future continuous tense is formed as "shall/will + be + verb-ing". With the subject "I", the traditionally correct form is "shall be coming".

◦ Correct: I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will be coming" is also continuous but uses "will" with "I"; Option 3 (shall be) best matches the original "I shall come".

• Option 2 "shall have come" is future perfect; Option 4 "will come" is simple future — neither is continuous.

NOTE

• Tense structures: Simple future = shall/will + V1; Future continuous = shall/will + be + V-ing; Future perfect = shall/will + have + V3.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

A majority of Indians prefer to use the Internet for ______________ booking and other financial services.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. accessing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accessing" means gaining or obtaining the use of / reaching (a service, data, etc.). People use the Internet for accessing booking and financial services. (पहुँच प्राप्त करना)

◦ Correct: ... prefer to use the Internet for accessing booking and other financial services.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "attending" (being present at), Option 3 "improving" (making better) and Option 4 "dispersing" (scattering) do not fit the idea of using online services.

NOTE

• "Access" as a verb is common in the context of technology: access a website, access your account, access information.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Only when the floods get _________ will world governments begin to act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. worse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the linking verb "get" we need an adjective, and the sense of the sentence (governments act only when the situation deteriorates) requires the comparative "worse". (और बदतर होना)

◦ Correct: Only when the floods get worse will world governments begin to act.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "frequently" is an adverb, which cannot follow "get" here.

• Options 1 "lucky" and 4 "gullible" do not suit the context of worsening floods.

NOTE

• "get + adjective" shows a change of state: get worse, get better, get tired, get ready. "Worse" is the comparative of "bad/badly".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Attract
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Repel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Attract" means to draw or pull towards oneself; to arouse interest. Its antonym is "repel", meaning to drive/push away or cause aversion. (आकर्षित करना का विलोम — विकर्षित करना)

◦ Example: Like poles of a magnet repel, while unlike poles attract.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "React" (to respond), Option 2 "Rear" (to bring up/back part) and Option 3 "Recur" (to happen again) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of attract: draw, allure, entice, fascinate. Antonyms: repel, repulse, disgust, put off.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. considered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Considered" here means thought of / regarded as. "To forgive an injury is often considered to be a sign of weakness" — i.e., people regard it that way. (समझा जाता है)

◦ Correct: To forgive an injury is often considered to be a sign of weakness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "given", Option 3 "allowed" and Option 4 "granted" do not fit the structure "considered to be".

• "Considered to be" is a standard passive collocation meaning "regarded as".

NOTE

• Common structure: "be considered (to be) + noun/adjective" = to be thought of as. Synonyms of consider: regard, deem, view, judge.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. strength.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage contrasts weakness with its opposite. Forgiveness is "really a sign of strength", because it takes a strong character to forgive. (शक्ति/सामर्थ्य)

◦ Correct: ... it is really a sign of strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The word "strength" directly contrasts with "weakness" mentioned just before, making it the logical choice.

• Options 1 "usefulness", 2 "intelligence" and 4 "aptitude" do not provide this contrast.

NOTE

• Look for contrast markers ("really", "but", "although") — they signal that the answer opposes the previous idea. Here weakness ↔ strength.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. vengeance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vengeance" means revenge / retaliation for a wrong. Being carried away "by resentment and hate into an act of vengeance" fits perfectly. (प्रतिशोध/बदला)

◦ Correct: ... to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of vengeance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "jurisprudence" (the study of law), Option 2 "overabundance" (excess) and Option 3 "noncompliance" (failure to obey) do not follow from "resentment and hate".

NOTE

• "Vengeance" links naturally with resentment and hate. Synonyms: revenge, retaliation, retribution, reprisal. Idiom: "with a vengeance" (with great force).

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. forgives.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The whole passage is about forgiveness. "The man who forgives an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him" restates the central theme. (क्षमा करता है)

◦ Correct: The man who forgives an injury proves himself to be the superior ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "achieves" (accomplishes), Option 3 "involves" (includes) and Option 4 "contrives" (plans cleverly) do not fit the idea of pardoning a wrong.

NOTE

• Maintain thematic consistency in cloze passages — the recurring idea here is forgiveness, so "forgives" is the natural fit.

question: Jallianwala Bagh is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amritsar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jallianwala Bagh is a public garden located in Amritsar, Punjab. It is the site of the infamous Jallianwala Bagh Massacre of 13 April 1919, when General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to open fire on an unarmed crowd gathered to protest the Rowlatt Act. (जलियाँवाला बाग — अमृतसर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The massacre took place on Baisakhi day and killed hundreds of innocent people.

• In protest, Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood, and Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920).

NOTE

• Amritsar is also home to the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib), the holiest shrine of Sikhism, founded by Guru Ram Das and completed by Guru Arjan Dev.

question: Children's Day in India is celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of _________.
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Dr. APJ. Abdul Kalam
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Children's Day in India is celebrated on 14 November to commemorate the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, who loved children and was fondly called "Chacha Nehru". (बाल दिवस — जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jawaharlal Nehru was born on 14 November 1889 in Allahabad.

• He authored famous books such as "The Discovery of India", "Glimpses of World History" and his Autobiography (Toward Freedom).

NOTE

• Teachers' Day (5 September) marks the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan; APJ Abdul Kalam's birthday (15 October) is observed as World Students' Day.

question: Both, Rajesh Prasanna and Rishabh Prasanna are associated with which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajesh Prasanna and Rishabh Prasanna are renowned Indian musicians associated with the flute (bansuri). They belong to the well-known Prasanna family of flautists. (बाँसुरी — फ्लूट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The flute (bansuri) is a wind instrument made of bamboo; it is closely linked with Lord Krishna in Indian tradition.

• Legendary Indian flautists include Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pannalal Ghosh.

NOTE

• Musical instruments are broadly of four types: string (tata), wind (sushira) such as flute, membrane/percussion (avanaddha) and solid/metallic (ghana).

question: The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana was implemented through which organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Employees Provident Fund Organisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY) was implemented through the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). Launched in October 2020, it aimed to incentivise employers to create new jobs and restore employment lost during the COVID-19 pandemic. (आत्मनिर्भर भारत रोज़गार योजना — EPFO)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under ABRY, the government subsidised the employees' and employers' EPF contributions for new employees.

• EPFO is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, managing provident fund, pension and insurance for organised-sector workers.

NOTE

• Related EPFO schemes: Employees' Provident Fund (EPF), Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI).

question: Which of the following was the mascot of the 37th National Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Moga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Moga", a lion cub, was the official mascot of the 37th National Games, held in Goa in 2023. The name reflects Goa's culture and the lion symbolises strength and pride. (37वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — शुभंकर मोगा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 37th National Games were held from 26 October to 9 November 2023 in Goa; Maharashtra topped the medal tally.

• The 38th National Games (2025) were hosted by Uttarakhand.

NOTE

• A mascot is a symbolic figure representing a sporting event, meant to promote goodwill and enthusiasm.

question: Which brick-made minaret holds the record for being the world's tallest tower at 73 metres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qutb Minar (India).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Qutb Minar in Delhi, at about 73 metres (approx. 72.5 m), is the tallest brick minaret in the world. Its construction was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (founder of the Delhi Sultanate) and completed by Iltutmish. (कुतुब मीनार — विश्व की सबसे ऊँची ईंट की मीनार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Qutb Minar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, built in the Indo-Islamic architectural style with red sandstone and marble.

• Nearby stands the famous Iron Pillar of Delhi, known for its rust-resistance.

NOTE

• Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

question: Vinod Kevin Bachan has been selected for the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar 2021, for his contribution to which Indian dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinod Kevin Bachan was selected for the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar 2021 for his contribution to the Odissi classical dance form. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खाँ युवा पुरस्कार — ओडिसी नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar is given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to young artists (below 40 years) in the fields of music, dance and drama.

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, characterised by the tribhanga posture and graceful movements.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following is NOT a drawback of the barter system?
option_1: Lack of a common unit of value
option_2: Surplus goods are replaced with other goods
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surplus goods are replaced with other goods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the barter system, goods are exchanged directly for goods. "Surplus goods being replaced (exchanged) with other goods" is actually how barter works, so it is NOT a drawback — it is a feature. (वस्तु विनिमय प्रणाली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Genuine drawbacks of barter include: double coincidence of wants, lack of a common unit/measure of value, difficulty in storing value, indivisibility of goods and difficulty in making deferred/contractual payments.

• Money was invented to overcome these limitations.

NOTE

• Functions of money: medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value and standard of deferred payment — precisely the problems that barter could not solve.

question: Chili peppers produce a burning sensation in any tissue with which they come into contact. What is the compound responsible for this?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Capsaicin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Capsaicin" is the active chemical compound in chili peppers that produces the burning/pungent sensation on contact with body tissue. (कैप्साइसिन — मिर्च का तीखापन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The pungency of chillies is measured on the Scoville Scale (SHU — Scoville Heat Units).

• Capsaicin is used in pepper sprays and in medicinal pain-relief creams.

NOTE

• Option 1 formic acid is found in ant/nettle stings; Option 2 acetic acid is present in vinegar; Option 3 lycopene gives tomatoes their red colour.

question: Identify the tributary of the Brahmaputra River from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Burhi Dihing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Burhi Dihing" (Buri Dihing) is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River, flowing through Assam. (बूढ़ी दिहिंग — ब्रह्मपुत्र की सहायक नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Major tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the Subansiri, Manas, Dhansiri, Kameng, Teesta and Burhi Dihing.

• The Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo in Tibet and Jamuna in Bangladesh; it rises from the Angsi Glacier near Mansarovar.

NOTE

• Option 2 Barakar is a tributary of the Damodar; Option 4 Hindan is a tributary of the Yamuna.

question: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) marked the beginning of:
option_1: French East India Company's rule in India
option_3: British East India company's rule in India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mughal's Rule in India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi (the last Sultan of the Lodi/Delhi Sultanate). Babur's victory marked the beginning of Mughal rule in India. (पानीपत का प्रथम युद्ध — मुगल शासन की शुरुआत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur used field artillery (cannons) and the Tulughma war strategy to defeat Ibrahim Lodi's larger army.

• This was one of the earliest battles in India to use gunpowder and firearms extensively.

NOTE

• Panipat battles: First (1526) – Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi; Second (1556) – Akbar/Bairam Khan vs Hemu; Third (1761) – Ahmad Shah Abdali vs the Marathas.

question: Which among the following dynasties originated from the Yueh-chih tribe of China?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kushanas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kushana dynasty originated from the Yueh-chih (Yuezhi) tribe of Central Asia/China. The Kushanas established a vast empire spanning Central Asia and northern India. (कुषाण वंश — यूची जनजाति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The greatest Kushana ruler was Kanishka (c. 127 CE), a patron of Mahayana Buddhism, who convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir.

• The Gandhara and Mathura schools of art flourished under the Kushanas.

NOTE

• Kanishka started the Saka era in 78 CE. The Gupta dynasty was indigenous (founded by Sri Gupta); the Satavahanas ruled the Deccan.

question: How many fundamental duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ten.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added ten (10) Fundamental Duties to the Constitution as Article 51A in a new Part IVA. (42वाँ संविधान संशोधन — 10 मूल कर्तव्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, inspired by the Constitution of the USSR.

• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty (duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6–14).

NOTE

• The 42nd Amendment is called the "Mini Constitution"; it also added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.

question: Limestone is composed of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is calcium carbonate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed mainly of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). (चूना-पत्थर — कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Limestone is the chief raw material for cement and is used in making quicklime (CaO) and slaked lime (Ca(OH)₂).

• Marble is a metamorphic form of limestone, also made of calcium carbonate.

NOTE

• Other CaCO₃ substances: chalk, marble, calcite and egg shells/sea shells. On heating, limestone gives lime and carbon dioxide: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.

question: The novel 'Pinjar' that was later converted into a motion picture was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amrita Pritam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The novel "Pinjar" (The Skeleton) was written by the eminent Punjabi writer and poet Amrita Pritam. It deals with the trauma of the Partition of India (1947), especially its impact on women. (पिंजर — अमृता प्रीतम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Pinjar" was made into a National Award-winning Hindi film (2003) directed by Chandraprakash Dwivedi.

• Amrita Pritam was the first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award (1956); she also received the Jnanpith Award and Padma Vibhushan. Her famous poem is "Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu".

NOTE

• Krishna Sobti ("Zindaginama"), Ismat Chughtai ("Lihaaf") and Dharamveer Bharati ("Gunahon Ka Devta") are other noted writers.

question: Who among the following social reformers ruled out the practice of Sati on the basis of Hindu religious texts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy campaigned against the practice of Sati, arguing on the basis of Hindu religious/scriptural texts that it had no sanction in ancient tradition. His efforts led to the abolition of Sati by Lord William Bentinck through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829. (राजा राम मोहन रॉय — सती प्रथा का विरोध)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828) and is regarded as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance / Modern India".

• He also opposed child marriage, polygamy and idol worship, and promoted women's rights and modern education.

NOTE

• The Mughal emperor Akbar granted him the title "Raja" — he carried it to England as an envoy, where he died in Bristol (1833).

question: How many covalent bonds are present between the constituent atoms in the molecules of Butane and Hexane, respectively?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 and 19.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Butane (C₄H₁₀) has 13 covalent bonds: 3 C–C bonds + 10 C–H bonds = 13.

• Hexane (C₆H₁₄) has 19 covalent bonds: 5 C–C bonds + 14 C–H bonds = 19.

◦ For an alkane CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, total bonds = (n−1) C–C bonds + (2n+2) C–H bonds = 3n. For butane (n=4) → 12? Let us verify: (4−1)=3 C–C, and 10 C–H → 3+10 = 13. For hexane (n=6): (6−1)=5 C–C, and 14 C–H → 5+14 = 19.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Butane and hexane are saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) containing only single covalent bonds.

• Alkanes follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

NOTE

• A covalent bond forms by the sharing of electron pairs between atoms. Carbon has a valency of 4, so each carbon forms four covalent bonds.

question: Which edition of 'Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana' has been announced in union budget 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.0.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union Budget 2023-24 announced the launch of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 (PMKVY 4.0) to skill lakhs of youth over the next three years. (प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना 4.0)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PMKVY is the flagship skill development scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), launched in 2015.

• PMKVY 4.0 emphasises new-age courses like coding, AI, robotics, drones and 3D printing.

NOTE

• Skill India Mission was launched on 15 July 2015 (observed as World Youth Skills Day), with PMKVY as its main component.

question: What is the term for the gradual, sequential changes in species composition in an ecosystem over time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Succession.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ecological succession" is the gradual, sequential change in the species composition of a community/ecosystem over time, until a stable climax community is reached. (पारिस्थितिक अनुक्रमण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Primary succession starts on a bare, lifeless area (e.g., bare rock) with pioneer species like lichens.

• Secondary succession occurs where a community was cleared but soil remains (e.g., after a fire or flood) and is faster.

NOTE

• Adaptation = adjustment to environment; Evolution = change in inherited traits over generations; Extinction = complete disappearance of a species. Only "succession" fits community-level change over time.

question: Which of the following classical dance styles manifests the element of sky?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the classical dances associated with the five elements (Pancha Bhoota), Kathakali is said to manifest the element of sky/space (Akasha). (कथकली — आकाश तत्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Association of dances with elements (as popularly stated): Bharatanatyam – Fire (Agni), Kuchipudi – Earth (Prithvi), Mohiniyattam – Air (Vayu), Odissi – Water (Jala) and Kathakali – Sky/Space (Akasha).

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama of Kerala, famous for its elaborate make-up, costumes and expressive facial abhinaya.

NOTE

• Kathakali usually depicts stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and is traditionally performed by male dancers.

question: Which of the following amendments, made in September 2023, is known as 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 128th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Women's Reservation Bill, known as the "Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam", was introduced in September 2023 as the 128th Constitutional Amendment Bill. It provides for the reservation of one-third (33%) of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. (नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It was the first bill passed in the new Parliament building.

• On enactment it became the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act; its implementation is linked to the next Census and delimitation exercise.

NOTE

• Reservation for women will initially be for 15 years and will also apply to seats reserved for SCs and STs.

question: Which state hosted the 6th edition of Khelo India Youth Games in 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 6th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games was hosted by Tamil Nadu in 2024 (held in Chennai, Madurai, Trichy and Coimbatore). (छठे खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally at the 2024 Games.

• The Khelo India Youth Games were launched in 2018 to promote sports at the grassroots and identify young talent.

NOTE

• Previous hosts: New Delhi (2018), Pune/Maharashtra (2019), Guwahati/Assam (2020), Panchkula/Haryana (2021), Madhya Pradesh (2022-23).

question: The Hugli industrial region is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hugli (Hooghly) industrial region is located in West Bengal, along the banks of the Hooghly River. It is one of the oldest industrial regions in India, centred around Kolkata. (हुगली औद्योगिक क्षेत्र — पश्चिम बंगाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The region is famous for the jute industry, along with cotton textiles, paper, chemicals and engineering.

• Its growth was aided by the port of Kolkata, availability of coal from the Damodar valley and cheap labour.

NOTE

• Major industrial regions of India: Mumbai-Pune, Hugli, Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Chhotanagpur, Vishakhapatnam-Guntur and Delhi-Meerut.

question: As per Census 2011, what is the average female literacy rate in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65.46%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the female literacy rate in India was 65.46% (approx. 65.5%). (जनगणना 2011 — महिला साक्षरता दर लगभग 65.46%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04%; male literacy was 82.14%.

• Kerala had the highest female literacy, while Rajasthan had the lowest among the major states.

NOTE

• Literacy rate = percentage of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding. Census 2011 was India's 15th National Census.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India describes a key feature of 'Universal Adult Franchise' that grants the right to vote to citizens, above the age of 18 years in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 326.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 326 of the Constitution provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage (Universal Adult Franchise), granting the right to vote to every citizen aged 18 years and above. (अनुच्छेद 326 — वयस्क मताधिकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

• Elections in India are conducted by the Election Commission of India under Article 324.

NOTE

• Article 352 deals with National Emergency; Article 315 with the Public Service Commissions (UPSC/SPSC); Article 367 with interpretation of the Constitution.
